forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred well south of WA extends a ridge over northern and western SA. The high drifts over waters well to the south of SA over the weekend, while a developing low pressure system and trough in WA move close to the SA border. The high drifts southeast of Tasmania by Monday as the low moves across western SA on Monday and northern SA on Tuesday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible light morning showers about the agricultural area. Possible showers or thunderstorms in the west, becoming more likely in the far northwest during the afternoon. Maximum temperatures below average, grading to above average in the northwest and far north. Moderate to fresh south to southeasterly winds, shifting east to northeasterly in the west.

Frost patches about the southeast. Possible showers or thunderstorms in the west, possibly extending into central districts during the afternoon. Maximum temperatures below average, grading to above average in the west. Moderate to fresh southeast to northeasterly winds, shifting southwest to southeasterly in the far west later.

Possible showers or thunderstorms about the pastoral districts and adjacent parts of the agricultural area. Maximum temperatures above average. East to northeasterly winds, freshening about western and central parts, ahead of a fresh southwest to southerly change moving across western parts during the day.

text.p: Possible showers or thunderstorms about the far north and northeast. Maximum temperatures above average in the east and far north, grading to below average in the southwest. Moderate to fresh northeast to northwesterly winds about eastern parts at first, with fresh southwest to southeasterly winds in the west. extending throughout during the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: Broadly less than 2 mm across the state. Falls increasing to 2 to 5 mm about the North West Pastoral and South East districts, with isolated falls of 5 to 10 mm possible about the far northwest and far southeast and of 10 to 20 mm with thunderstorms.
